races.name: Champagne Pommery Brut Rose Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer with six recent runs mostly over 10f on similar going, placed five times in last six; Kieran Shoemark takes the ride and this trip suits his staying profile, though he is a natural hold-up horse who will need Gemini Man to set a true enough pace.|
runners_data.comment: Falcon Nine has been runner-up three times in his last six starts, most recently 11 days ago, and arrives fit and well-handicapped on our rating; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, and from stall seven carries 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Good and has strong placed form on similar ground; a genuine hold-up horse by nature but is likely to find herself travelling closer to midfield than she would prefer in this shape, slightly undermining her best tactical scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Samra Star arrives here on the back of a win last time out and a second before that, boasting experience over today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that eighth earlier in her recent form hints at some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Miners Gamble
runners_data.note: Recent form is poor — consecutive below-par finishes on Tapeta and Soft ground — and his natural closer's style will be compromised by being pushed into midfield given how many rear-trackers are in this field; Luke Morris holds the booking but the form gives little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Miners Gamble has run over today's trip and going before and, returning on a sharp 13-day turnaround, is fit enough to go close; our rating of 57 ranks him fourth of the seven, though winless in his last six starts, that lack of a win is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Has winning form over 8f on Good and a solid recent placed record on similar conditions; Jim Goldie's runner carries the penalty for experience but, despite being a true hold-up horse, may find herself tracking closer to midfield than ideal, which slightly blunts her best finisher's angle.|
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out makes him hard to fancy despite a win one start back, and a struggling trainer strike-rate of 5% over the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence. He has run over today's trip and going, and 11 days between runs suggests he's fit.

runners_data.name: Liberty Looming
runners_data.note: All recent form has come over much longer distances (13f-17f), making the 1m1f trip here an obvious question mark; as a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield by the field's composition, she faces both a style-fit and a distance concern that makes her hard to favour.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Liberty Looming faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp seven-day turnaround in good enough order from stall two carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and has a modest record without a win in recent starts; Lexie Clarkson's 7lb claim helps on the weight, but a tendency to empty late is a significant negative in a race likely run at a controlled pace where the finish may be sharp.|
runners_data.comment: Toy Soldier has shown real consistency at this level, finishing second in two of his last six starts, and he returns in good order just 18 days after his last outing — experience over today's trip and going is a further asset. The risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, he has won twice recently over longer trips including on Good ground and has shown he can dominate from the front; Jack Nicholls takes the 3lb claim and, with a completely uncontested lead available, he is the shape's key reference point throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Gemini Man ran second last time out in a pleasing return to form, though a pulled up effort two starts back is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and his two wins in his last six starts suggest he retains ability, but 130 lb is a stern test.

races.paceDynamic: Gemini Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m1f handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest him for the lead, he can dictate a measured, controlled gallop on Good turf at Musselburgh. The remainder of the field — Falcon Nine, Samra Star, Miners Gamble, Approaching Dawn, Liberty Looming, and Toy Soldier — are all natural hold-up or rear-tracking types, meaning the early sections will be straightforward for Gemini Man to control. The field does hold more genuine hold-up horses than the map can place at the back; Samra Star, Miners Gamble, Approaching Dawn, and Liberty Looming are all true closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than is natural for them, with only Falcon Nine and Toy Soldier able to settle comfortably in the positions shown. This race shape — a lone leader dictating an uncontested, honest-but-not-extreme pace on Good ground — favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finishing effort from midfield, particularly those with proven form on similar Good going over this sort of trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gemini Man Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man leads from the outset and sets a controlled, even gallop that gradually empties out the hold-up horses before they can wind up.
scenarios.body: Gemini Man controls every stage, conserving enough energy to see out the 1m1f on Good ground, and the fractured finishing efforts of the closers — many forced closer than ideal — fail to reel him in before the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man's pace is just quick enough to suit a strong-finishing hold-up horse who can produce a sustained run from well back.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer who settles sweetly in the early stages produces a sweeping run over the final two furlongs, catching a tiring Gemini Man near the line on ground that rewards stamina and rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough that a horse tracking in the middle-third produces the quickest finish without needing to come from far back.
scenarios.body: With the hold-up runners crowded into midfield rather than settled at the rear, a horse who slots into fourth or fifth and keeps tabs on Gemini Man produces the most economical run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man sets too strong a pace for the trip and ties up inside the final furlong, handing the initiative to anything with a late kick.
scenarios.body: Given Gemini Man's recent form at longer distances and his age, a slight miscalculation in pace-judgment could see him weaken late, opening the door for the freshest finisher to grab the prize.

watchPoints.text: Gemini Man — watch whether Jack Nicholls allows him to dictate entirely on his own terms from the first furlong; if he is allowed a soft lead, the entire field's chances of catching him are significantly reduced.

Falcon Nine — watch his early positioning; Kieran Shoemark may attempt to track Gemini Man more closely than his hold-up tag implies, and if he gets a good stalking berth he becomes the most dangerous challenger.

Liberty Looming — watch for signs of an awkward early pace adjustment, as a horse used to 13f-17f races settling into a 1m1f contest may either pull too hard or fail to quicken when required in the final stages.

Toy Soldier — watch the final furlong specifically; if the pace has been truly steady throughout, her tendency to fade may be less pronounced, but a faster-than-expected tempo will expose that weakness earlier.

Approaching Dawn — watch the split between actual hold-up types at the back and how compressed the midfield becomes; if runners bunch tightly behind Gemini Man, she may be left with little room to produce her run when it matters.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Barnaby Rudge
runners_data.note: Two wins from the front at 5f on Soft and Standard give him genuine each-way claims here; James Fanshawe sends him 41 days fresh which is a positive trainer pattern, and he wears hood headgear — however, he must share the lead with My Mate Fitz, which could prove costly late.|

runners_data.name: Minster Man
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's speedy juveniles are well-suited to sharp 5f tracks, and his sole run produced a closing second on Good ground — the most directly relevant form in this field; Paul Mulrennan fits the course well and the hold-up style is tailor-made for this contested-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: My Mate Fitz
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves takes the ride on a horse whose form reads 4-6 over 5-6f, suggesting raw ability without the composure to sustain it; he has faced stronger company than most rivals here but the front-running role in a head-to-head duel with Barnaby Rudge is a tough assignment on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Sod Hall Lane
runners_data.note: A complete unknown on debut for Declan Carroll, who has had one winner from ten runners in the last 14 days; the unknown style tag means he could land anywhere in the tactical picture, and apprentice Zak Wheatley will need a clean break to make use of whatever ability he brings to the track.|

runners_data.name: Faith In Florence
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has finished second and fourth in two 6f runs on Good ground, so dropping to 5f is a slight query — but the prominent style and Kieran Shoemark's booking suggest connections are confident; her best form came in the 2f run, and a sharp Musselburgh 5f with a hot early pace is the right environment to test whether she stays in touch.|

races.paceDynamic: Barnaby Rudge and My Mate Fitz are both confirmed front-runners and will dispute the lead from the off over this sharp Musselburgh 5f on Good ground, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a lone leader dictating terms. Barnaby Rudge has won twice from the front and arrives in form, while My Mate Fitz has shown early speed before fading, suggesting the pace pressure will be real but may cost both horses late. Faith In Florence and Minster Man will be tracking from prominent to hold-up positions, hoping the front-runners stretch the field and leave them with a clear late run. This contested pace shape on a flat, galloping 5f track favours closers and prominent horses who travel smoothly into the race and have the finishing kick to capitalise once the duelling leaders tie each other up — Minster Man and Faith In Florence fit that profile best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Pacesetters
scenarios.trigger: If Barnaby Rudge and My Mate Fitz push each other hard from the gates and set a genuine clip, leaving both vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The early duel saps the reserves of both front-runners, opening the race up for a horse who has settled just off the pace and can deliver a sustained finish; Musselburgh's flat 5f rewards that style directly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If My Mate Fitz dwells or misses the break, allowing Barnaby Rudge to stride clear uncontested and dictate a controlled, measured gallop.
scenarios.body: Without a rival pressing him, Barnaby Rudge can run his own race from the front, conserving enough energy to fight off challengers; his two wins from the front on similar ground make him the standout beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but the field fans wide and the leaders hang on through superior class or fitness advantage.
scenarios.body: Barnaby Rudge's two wins suggest he handles a hard-run race better than his rivals might expect, and if the finish compresses rather than strings out, hold-up horses find themselves short of room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Sod Hall Lane shows natural early pace or tactical versatility on debut and outguns the exposed runners with a fresh performance.
scenarios.body: Unexposed two-year-olds with unknown styles can exploit races where the known pace horses burn each other out; Declan Carroll's yard has the tools to produce a ready debutant, and the small field of five limits traffic risks.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Barnaby Rudge or My Mate Fitz blinks first leaving the stalls — whoever misses the break effectively gifts a soft lead to the other, transforming the race shape from contested to controlled in an instant.

Minster Man's hold-up style in a field of only five runners means Paul Mulrennan has very little cover; if the field spreads across the track early, he could find himself three or four lengths adrift with limited draught.

Faith In Florence has run exclusively at 6f and the drop to 5f at Musselburgh is an untested trip — if she is outpaced in the opening two furlongs by the front-runners, Shoemark may struggle to bridge the gap late.

Sod Hall Lane's debut means there is genuine uncertainty about stall behaviour and early positioning — in a five-runner race with two known leaders, any interference or awkward exit from the unknown debutant could disrupt the shape of the race from the first stride.

Barnaby Rudge is fitted with hood headgear again after wearing it in both wins — any sign it is having less effect on his concentration than in those earlier races would be a flag that his on-pace dominance may not repeat.

races.name: Copper Blossom Ladies Day Nursery Selling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Extended Order
runners_data.note: Beaten favourite last time out at 7f on Good having also won over the trip; Joanna Mason's regular partner Daniel Muscutt takes over, and the finishing fade warning is significant — Eve Johnson Houghton's filly may not stay strongly enough to peg back a controlled front-runner if she gets no pace to aim at.
runners_data.comment: Extended Order landed a win three starts back and returns on a sharp 21-day turnaround with distance experience in his favour, drawing stall 3 carrying 135 lb; the risk is that he has been unplaced in his last two starts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's juvenile showed a progressive profile (1W3P in last seven at 7f on Good) but her naturally deep hold-up style is compromised here; with this small field of closers, she is pushed into an uncharacteristic midfield role that blunts her chance unless the pace blows up late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last of five on our figures, Amantha faces a stiff ask, though her recent form has improved markedly — a winner three starts back, second two starts back, and third last time out — and she has run over today's distance and going before, returning on a sharp seven-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Bella Lucia
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's filly has an undefined running style (U) which is actually a tactical asset in a race with one pace-setter — she can slot wherever suits — though her form has been over shorter (5-6f) and this 7f Good ground debut for the trip is an open question on stamina.
runners_data.comment: Bella Lucia has shown consistent placing ability, finishing third two of her last three starts, and has run over today's trip before — she comes here just 15 days fresh and looks a solid danger. The main risk is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this Roger Fell-trained filly who has posted two 7f Good-ground seconds recently, showing genuine aptitude for the trip, but five runs over the course-and-distance without a win points to a horse who finds one too good rather than one who wins from the front.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, Bigalo has posted back-to-back runner-up finishes and has experience over today's trip and conditions — he's winless in his last five but the placed form is solid, and our rating has him narrowly on top here.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's blinker-wearing front-runner has a 7f Good-ground win to her name and the Style Fit flag (0.93) reflects that she naturally leads rather than races prominently — in a field this small she will almost certainly seize the front and test whether her controlled gallop is enough to repel rivals.
runners_data.comment: Bluestone Lady arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a live threat at 129 lb from stall 4; the main risk is that unplaced run two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Bluestone Lady is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine rival to press her, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over Musselburgh's flat seven furlongs. Extended Order, Amantha, and Bigalo are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured and Bluestone Lady can conserve energy through the middle section before quickening into the two-furlong pole. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear, and Amantha — a genuine closer — has been mapped to midfield precisely because there is no room for multiple horses to race truly detached; Extended Order and Bigalo are most likely to actually secure the rearmost berths. A lone, uncontested pace-setter over a flat track on Good ground in a small field strongly favours horses who can either lead or race prominently tracking that moderate gallop, with closers needing the pace to lift sharply in the final two furlongs to have enough ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bluestone Lady Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Bluestone Lady bowls along in front unchallenged and sets a measured, honest pace that leaves nothing fresh to come at her.
scenarios.body: Bluestone Lady has won at 7f on Good at this trip and uses her blinkers to concentrate, and an uncontested lead on a flat, galloping track means she can dictate tempo and stretch the field before the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Bluestone Lady closely and pounces in the final furlong as the leader ties up.
scenarios.body: A tidy-tempo race with one pacemaker can leave a close-tracking type perfectly poised for a late lunge, and Bella Lucia — while unproven at 7f — has the tactical flexibility of an unknown style to slot in second.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bluestone Lady sets a faster-than-expected gallop early and ties up inside the final furlong, leaving room for hold-up horses to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Extended Order has winning form at 7f on Good and showed ability to close from off the pace, and Bigalo's repeated second-place finishes at 7f on Good suggest she can produce late energy if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Bluestone Lady goes off too fast or the slow early gallop causes a bunched, sprint finish from the two-furlong mark.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish in a small field would randomise the result, but Bigalo's two recent second-place finishes at 7f on Good show she handles a scrappy finish better than most.

watchPoints.text: Bluestone Lady — watch whether she gets away cleanly from the stalls; if she misses the break, this entire race shape collapses and the field becomes a free-for-all sprint from the rear.
Extended Order — the finishing-fade tag is critical to monitor in-running; if she is not travelling easily into the final quarter-mile, she is likely to be beaten despite superior form figures.

Amantha — watch her position at the two-furlong marker; if she is still further back than midfield, her true closer's style is being fully negated and her redistribution onto the map understates how far she is out of position.

Bigalo — monitor whether Joanna Mason attempts to ride her closer to the pace than usual given the small field; her two recent 7f Good second places both came from midfield, and any change in tactics could alter the shape significantly.

Bella Lucia — an unknown style horse in a small, slow-pace field can end up racing greenly or awkwardly behind a lone leader; watch for William Pyle settling her quickly, as that will determine whether she is a factor or a passenger.

races.name: Champagne Pommery Cuvee Louise Gold Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5yo in solid form (placed in 4 of last 5), handles good going well (12 of 15 runs on similar ground), steps up to 7f from a run of 6f starts and the extra furlong could suit; Jack Nicholls (3lb claim) adds value and Iain Jardine's yard is firing (4/24 T14).
runners_data.comment: Jonny Concrete arrives on the back of a win last time out, is fit on a 14-day turnaround, and has experience over today's trip and conditions — our rating of 90 marks him as a strong threat. The main risk is whether he can defy a testing burden of 138 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Gweedore
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose recent form figures (7-0-4-0-0) offer little encouragement, and the 32-day break adds uncertainty; only 6 of 15 runs on similar going have yielded any meaningful return and Tom Eaves has limited material to work with here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Gweedore nonetheless rates 96 on our figures — top of these eleven — and returns after 32 days having run over today's distance and going before; stall three and 137 lb to carry are the questions here.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4yo has finished 5th-7th in all five recent runs, all on good ground, suggesting a horse who finds a level but struggles to win from a hold-up berth when the pace isn't truly severe; Tudhope's quality is a plus but the form string gives no cause for confidence.
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround in good order, with our rating of 90 marking him out as a live threat in this field — the risk is that he's winless in his last five starts, suggesting the breakthrough remains elusive.

runners_data.name: One Night Thunder
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground but that strike rate is solitary — this 6yo's true preference is to come from off the pace, and with the field stacked with hold-up types he is likely to be shuffled into a more forward position than suits him; treat his chance with caution in a shape where the early pace does not truly test the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, One Night Thunder does at least bring distance-and-going experience to the table and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround; however, a third three starts back is his only bright note in a largely moderate recent sequence, and 132 lb from stall 10 adds little comfort.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Has three wins on good ground over 7f including an impressive recent success, giving Jim Goldie's filly strong course-and-distance credentials; however, her natural hold-up style means she's been mapped to midfield, and Paul Mulrennan will need to adapt tactically rather than relying on a straightforward late run.
runners_data.comment: Native Honey has won twice in his last six starts, but only a fifth last time out makes him hard to fancy, and a trainer firing at just 5% recently compounds the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, which counts for something.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's mount has an excellent record on good ground (8 from 8 recorded runs on similar) and the form figures over 7f are solid, with a course win included; sits at the back of the field naturally but would benefit most if the tempo genuinely stretches the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Zarvali showed useful form when third two starts back and a winner four starts back, but a seventh last time out is harder to ignore; he has distance and going experience to call upon, though 129 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator by nature for Jim Goldie who has placed in three of her last five but is positioned in midfield on the map due to field congestion at the rear; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is attractive but the style compromise in a pace-controlled race tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Ashen is hard to fancy for all that he has experience of today's trip and going, draws stall one, and returns on a quick turnaround with a win in his last six starts to his name.

runners_data.name: Eagle Bay
runners_data.note: The standout pace-setter, unbeaten in two starts, winning his last two over 7f on good and soft; Sean D Bowen takes over from a hat-trick chasing position and the 41-day break is the only note of caution, though his form is compact and he has only had three runs total.
runners_data.comment: Eagle Bay arrives on the back of two wins in his last three starts, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour, but carrying 136 lb from stall 11, our rating puts him well below the field's leading lights, making him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's well-credentialled 3yo has already won over 7f on good ground and carries the joint-top weight; Kieran Shoemark is a significant booking and the 49-day break is the one question mark, but a horse who gets into a prominent tracking position off a controlled gallop is ideally placed in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Passing Thought has won twice in her last five starts, including a victory two starts back, and has run over today's distance and going — a trainer firing at 26% over the past fortnight adds strong confidence; the concern is whether 49 days off has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Vixey
runners_data.note: A prominent-racing 6yo whose last five runs have all come over 8f, making this step back to 7f a potential query; the trainer's 0 of 1 T14 strike rate and the step down in trip introduce enough uncertainty to temper enthusiasm, despite a respectable overall win record.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a second two runs back shows she retains ability; Vixey has run over today's trip and going, and 10 days since her latest outing leaves her fresh, but her most recent run was unplaced and she ranks eighth of eleven on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Augustus Gloop
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo has been consistent in placed efforts but all five recent runs are at Southwell on standard surface — the jump to turf on good ground at Musselburgh is a genuine unknown; Daniel Muscutt is a capable booking and the prominent style fits the pace shape perfectly if he handles the going change.
runners_data.comment: Augustus Gloop showed a win and a second in recent starts but has since dropped to finishes of sixth and seventh, and was only fourth last time out; he has run over today's trip and steps back in from stall five carrying 133 lb, though that dip in form gives pause.

races.paceDynamic: Eagle Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Jonny Concrete, Passing Thought, Augustus Gloop, and Vixey likely to press from a prominent position, the pace should be genuine but not suicidal — Sean D Bowen can dictate terms at a rhythm that suits Eagle Bay's profile given the small competitive field up front. Jonny Concrete and Passing Thought are the most dangerous flanking presences, though neither is likely to force a scorching gallop, meaning the front two furlongs will be controlled rather than frantic. The field contains significantly more hold-up horses than the track map can accommodate at the rear: One Night Thunder, Native Honey, and Ashen are true hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield, meaning their natural late delivery may be compromised and their chances in a shape that requires genuine positional flexibility are discounted accordingly. This race shape — a controlled pace set by an uncontested leader — favours prominently-raced horses who can track the gallop and pounce entering the final two furlongs, rather than genuine closers whose late runs depend on a strong, truly contested early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eagle Bay Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Eagle Bay goes clear and dictates a steady-to-fair gallop, allowing trackers to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Eagle Bay leads in his own time, giving Passing Thought and Jonny Concrete a dream stalking position just off the pace with cover; entering the final furlong, the horses who have travelled comfortably in the slipstream have the energy advantage over true hold-up types who cannot deliver their natural late surge from midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the tracking prominent horses deliver a sustained challenge from two furlongs out and overwhelm Eagle Bay.
scenarios.body: Passing Thought or Augustus Gloop, having tracked Eagle Bay at close range, push past in the final furlong as the leader's momentum fades after controlling the race; this scenario rewards the horses with the best cruising speed and class within the OR 80-85 band.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Benefit From Farther Back
scenarios.trigger: If Eagle Bay sets a stronger gallop than anticipated and the pace genuinely tests every runner.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo would open up a gap for horses further back to reel in tired leaders, giving the redistributed hold-up types a realistic chance of delivering their natural finishing kick despite being mapped ahead of their preferred position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives All Challenges
scenarios.trigger: If Eagle Bay bowls along comfortably and the prominent chasers are unable to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With a clear lead and a rhythm of his own choosing on good ground over a trip he has already won on, Eagle Bay simply refuses to be caught as rivals fail to find their expected acceleration; this is least likely given the competitive OR ratings of the prominent types but cannot be dismissed given his unbeaten record at this distance.

watchPoints.text: Eagle Bay (Sean D Bowen) — watch whether he is allowed to dictate without pressure from Jonny Concrete or Passing Thought jumping out quickly, as his ability to control the tempo entirely determines the shape of this race.

Passing Thought (Kieran Shoemark) — 49 days off the track for Ed Walker's yard; watch the market moves and watch how sharply he comes out of the stalls, as a sluggish break from a prominent horse in this shape is costly.

Augustus Gloop (Daniel Muscutt) — all five career runs have come on artificial/standard ground at Southwell, making this turf debut on good ground a significant unknown; watch early betting to gauge stable confidence.

Native Honey and One Night Thunder — both are natural hold-up horses forced into a midfield berth by field composition; watch how their jockeys position in the first two furlongs, as any attempt to drop back to their true position will leave too much to do at Musselburgh's sharp 7f layout.

Zarvali (Joanna Mason) — an 8-from-8 record on similar going is a notable stat; watch whether she is able to find a clear run entering the final two furlongs, as her style depends entirely on getting a clean passage late.

races.name: Champagne Pommery Brut Royal Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer for Barron/Pyle on Good 5f (three thirds in similar going), but a genuine hold-up type who needs a strong pace to close into — the controlled fractions Big Fun is likely to set make this format less than ideal for him.
runners_data.comment: Jer Batt has finished third three times in his last five starts and returns on a quick turnaround just seven days after his latest effort, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; winless in recent starts, but our rating of 93 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes the ride for O'Meara, and this horse has an excellent record in similar going (13 of 15 runs) with two wins and six places; a hold-up style demands a real gallop but she has the tactical versatility to track if needed and should hit the board.
runners_data.comment: Tiva ran third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her key experience; winless in her last six starts, though, and that lack of a win remains the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a solid recent record at 5f on Good ground — two seconds and a third from his last five comparable runs — and Paul Mulrennan gives him a professional handler up front; his natural forward-going style suits the shape this race creates best.
runners_data.comment: Montezuma has been knocking on the door in recent starts — second last time out and third two starts back — and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the worry is his trainer is in a lean spell at just 5% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Big Fun
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Kevin Ryan who sets the entire race up from the front; racing off a 68-day break is worth noting and the STYLE_FIT flag is assigned because his map position is actually on role, but the layoff means fitness must be assumed rather than proven — if he does lead freely his tactical advantage is significant.
runners_data.comment: Big Fun won four starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating puts him well clear of his official mark — strong credentials for a bold show from stall one. The main risk is a return from 68 days off.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with a remarkable sequence of five consecutive second places, all on Good ground at 5-6f, for Jim Goldie; displayed to midfield on the map because the field is rear-heavy, but her natural instinct is to come from off the pace — she needs more fractions than Big Fun alone is likely to create.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite a string of runner-up finishes, Woohoo faces a stiff ask ranked fifth of six on our figures, and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going, at least.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: John Ryan's lightly-weighted three-year-old has mixed recent form figures and her last five runs have all been on Good ground without a win; she is a natural hold-up type working from a compressed midfield position in this map, and the STYLE_FIT discount is merited given her pattern and the unfavourable pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a best recent finish of fourth, Ecclefechan makes little appeal ranked last of six on our figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; 120 lb from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Big Fun is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival prepared to push for the lead, is expected to bowl along comfortably from the gates and control every fraction on this flat Musselburgh 5f. That uncontested, sustainable tempo plays directly into the hands of the prominent-to-midfield horse that tracks the leader without burning energy, leaving those held up at the rear relying on others to create enough pace to close onto. The field actually contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Woohoo and Ecclefechan are genuine closers forced toward midfield on the map, and while Montezuma may attempt to go with Big Fun, the pace lead is unlikely to be seriously challenged from the off. This shape — a lone leader setting a controlled, honest-but-not-pressured gallop — favours a prominent or tracking racer that travels smoothly within the race and can quicken off the turn, not the true hold-up type dependent on a strong pace being set in front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Big Fun Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Big Fun secures an uncontested lead and the pace remains honest but controlled throughout the 5f.
scenarios.body: Big Fun dictates every fraction without pressure, keeping the tempo moderate enough to preserve his stamina and make it very hard for true hold-up horses to close; a prominent tracker that travels fluidly behind him is the profile most likely to threaten at the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If Montezuma or a forward-positioned horse travels smoothly just behind Big Fun and delivers a sharper finishing kick.
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace means there is a genuine gear to find in the final furlong, and a horse sitting second or third with cover can pounce off the bend; Montezuma's recent 5f Good form and repeated placed efforts make him the natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns faster than expected and genuine closers get the stronger gallop they need to close.
scenarios.body: Woohoo's relentless placed record on Good 5f suggests she can finish powerfully if the tempo suits, and Jer Batt has the profile to pick up late; however, both are mapping out of their natural deepest position and the pace is unlikely to be truly strong enough to gift them a winning run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If there is an incident early, interference across the field, or Big Fun misses the break and the race breaks up unexpectedly.
scenarios.body: Ecclefechan, lowest-rated and lightest-weighted, would benefit from any scenario that scrambles the tempo and removes Big Fun's advantage; with 21 days since her last run she is fresh but her recent form figures offer limited grounds for confidence.

watchPoints.text: Big Fun's 68-day absence is the key unknown — watch the early-morning market for any drift that could signal a fitness concern from Kevin Ryan's yard before accepting the race-shape prediction built around him.

Woohoo and Ecclefechan are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield; if the pace is truly steady they will be hunting a gap that never opens, and both carrying the REDISTRIBUTED tag means their mapped position overstates their likely running position.

Montezuma attempts to go forward and match Big Fun early — if he pushes hard to dispute the lead rather than settle just behind, the tempo will rise sharply and the race shape changes entirely from controlled-pace to pressured sprint, benefiting closers.

Tiva's headgear (tv — visor) and Jer Batt's hood (p — hood) are both active; headgear changes or continuations at this venue on Good ground at 5f can occasionally trigger unexpected forward moves — watch both in the stalls and first furlong for any positional surprises.

races.name: Brodie Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 11f and 12f on Standard ground with Luke Morris, now stepping up to 1m5f which on pedigree should suit; Sir Mark Prescott's record with progressive stayers is formidable and this horse's prominent racing style places it ideally to exploit Willow Wood's likely controlled tempo — 7 days since last run is tight but Prescott rarely brings horses back too soon.
runners_data.comment: Roc De Fer arrives in cracking nick, winning his last two starts and with his trainer firing at 31% over the past fortnight. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 80 marks him out as the one to beat, though the 141 lb burden is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with strong Good-ground form at 16f, recording a win and multiple places at this sort of trip — but this horse is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position at the rear of the field is unavailable in a seven-runner race with one front-runner, so the race shape is working against its preferred style despite the obvious distance credentials.
runners_data.comment: Simple Star shaped with promise when second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going bolsters his claims under 139 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must find more on recent form.

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old placed on Good ground at 13f twice in its last five runs; Greg Fairley's mount has a genuine hold-up profile and will need the pace to be honest enough to bring its finishing effort into play over this longer trip — 27 days since last run is not a concern with two recent placing runs at comparable distances.
runners_data.comment: Consistently hitting the frame — third last time out and a second three starts back — Sure And Stedfast arrives on a good freshness angle at 27 days, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 74 suggests he's ahead of his official mark; the risk is he's yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tommy's Promise
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with multiple wins at 10f on Standard ground, stepping up sharply in trip after 126 days off — the layoff is the key flag here, and Tom Eaves will need to judge whether the horse has the fitness to sustain prominent racing over 1m5f after such a break despite the horse's bold front-running tendencies at shorter.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 126 days makes Tommy's Promise hard to trust here, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff task; ninth last time out compounds the concern. He has run over today's trip and going, and two wins in his last five starts show there is ability to unearth if fit.

runners_data.name: Alnayef
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old won at 13f on Good ground recently and has placed form at this sort of trip, but like Simple Star it is a hold-up horse by nature and Paul Mulrennan will find itself further forward than ideal in a seven-runner field with one genuine pace-setter — its Good-ground record (7/15 similar-going runs) is also more modest than the trip credentials suggest.
runners_data.comment: Alnayef showed up well with a third last time out and was a winner two starts back, but the trainer's current 5% strike rate over the last 14 days is a concern, and he carries a hefty 136 lb here.

runners_data.name: Willow Wood
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and Kieran Shoemark should lead from the outset; it won over 12f on Soft going and has form in competitive races, but its recent record on Good ground shows 0 wins and 0 places from two runs, and it is rated [STYLE_FIT=0.92] in the sense that uncontested leadership is its one strong card — any challenge from Tommy's Promise or Roc De Fer could expose its limitations.
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures and carrying 132 lb, Willow Wood faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a win two starts back and has previous experience on today's going; the trainer's 26% strike rate over the past fortnight offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Much
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old placed at 12f on Standard going last time and has Daniel Muscutt aboard; it has shown improvement in its last outing and the step up to 1m5f on Good turf could be the key to unlocking its potential, though as a hold-up type it depends on the pace being genuine and its Good-ground figures (2/4 similar runs) suggest the surface is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying 130 lb, Much has run over today's trip and going before, and his rating of 72 edges his official mark — making him a lively danger. The main risk is he's winless in his last four starts.

races.paceDynamic: Willow Wood is the one confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead, Kieran Shoemark should be able to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop over this 1m5f trip on Good ground at Musselburgh. With only Tommy's Promise and Roc De Fer as prominent types capable of tracking up, the early pace is unlikely to be brutal, meaning the complexion of the race — steady early, with pressure building in the straight — will suit those who can settle close to the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a flat-out sprint. The hold-up runners (Much, Sure And Stedfast, Simple Star, Alnayef) will need the pace to be honest enough to bring their finishing efforts into play, but with Willow Wood controlling tempo from the front, that is not guaranteed. This race shape strongly favours prominent or pace-stalking profiles who can travel within a length or two of Willow Wood and exploit any early conservatism, with deep closers carrying meaningful risk of finding the pace insufficient to reel in the leaders. Note: the field contains more hold-up types than can be accommodated naturally at the rear — Simple Star and Alnayef are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield precisely because there is insufficient room at the back of the field, and they may struggle to race authentically in this relatively small field with a single front-runner controlling tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Willow Wood controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Willow Wood leads at a measured, unchallenged gallop and the hold-up runners never get sufficient pace to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Shoemark sets a comfortable tempo, the race stays tactical and those tracking close to the leader are best placed to pounce in the straight; prominent and pace-stalking types have first run on the hold-up horses who are left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent duo overhaul leader
scenarios.trigger: If Roc De Fer or Tommy's Promise track Willow Wood throughout and wear her down in the final two furlongs as the pace quickens.
scenarios.body: Sir Mark Prescott's Roc De Fer brings strong recent form (back-to-back wins) and the stamina to grind over this trip, while Tommy's Promise has won over 10f and may appreciate the step up in distance; both are ideally placed to pounce once the front-runner ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses finish strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stronger than expected and creates enough of a true test to allow finishing horses to close meaningfully in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sure And Stedfast and Much have both placed at this type of distance on Good going and carry enough raw ability to reel in a tired leader if the pace plays into their hands; however, both Simple Star and Alnayef are racing somewhat out of their natural role and their redistribution into midfield makes their involvement in this scenario structurally weaker.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race falls apart, shock result
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely mid-race, creating a messy stop-start contest where form lines break down.
scenarios.body: In a race with a sole front-runner setting a dawdle and no one willing to take it up, the race could degenerate into a sprint finish that rewards a horse with raw speed rather than stamina; outsider chances materialise if hold-up types are caught flat-footed from the rear in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Willow Wood's sectionals from the front — if Shoemark allows an exceptionally slow early gallop, the hold-up horses Simple Star, Alnayef and Much will be left with a genuine closing challenge as the field will bunch turning for home and sprint rather than grind.

Tommy's Promise returns after a 126-day absence stepping up sharply in trip — watch whether Tom Eaves pitches it forward immediately or conserves energy, as the fitness question could unravel a prominent run at this distance.

Roc De Fer's weight (141lbs) is the highest in the field and Sir Mark Prescott's seven-day turnaround should be noted — if the horse carries the burden well early, it is positioned to be the most dangerous challenger to any leader on current form.

Simple Star and Alnayef are both true hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the race shape — watch how quickly Nicholls and Mulrennan can thread them through if the pace finally quickens in the straight, as a messy passage could cost either runner a placing.

Sure And Stedfast has run 27 days fresh and has placings on Good ground at 13f — if Greg Fairley gets a smooth passage from the rear, the form figures suggest it could outrun its odds if the pace turns honest in the final half-mile.

races.name: Muirhall Energy Breath Of Fresh Energy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner who won twice at 7f on good ground recently and is firmly in form (1-1-3 in last five at this trip); Ruth Carr sends her here 13 days after a run and she wears headgear — expect her to stride on from the front and her big STYLE_FIT score reflects she could struggle if denied her natural lead.|
runners_data.comment: Filey Beach showed smart form when third three starts back and a winner four starts back, and he arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going from stall one on 135 lb; the concern is his two more recent below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's six-year-old has live claims on this card — her trainer has 5 winners from 10 runners in the last 14 days — and a course-winning run at 7f on good ground backs her prominent racing style here; she has been placed at this trip on good and should sit right behind Filey Beach.|
runners_data.comment: Keep Me Stable arrives with distance and going experience in her favour, and a win five starts back gives her a proven route to the frame; the risk is that her last two outings — unplaced and then eighth — suggest she needs to rediscover that form sharpish.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: John Ryan has had a quiet 14 days (0/4) and Luke Morris takes the ride on this hold-up filly who has placed in four of her last five starts without getting her head in front; she needs more pace than Filey Beach is likely to generate to close enough ground from her deep position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Chloe's Courage faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and was third two starts back, suggesting she isn't entirely without ability.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old is a genuine closer who arrives just seven days after her last run wearing headgear and with five places from recent outings on good ground; she has been mapped to midfield because the hold-up berths are full — her true inclination is to come from off the pace, which will be harder to execute in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Misemerald nevertheless arrives in decent nick just seven days after finishing second, and has run over today's distance and going before — but with an official mark of 46 and ranked fifth of six on our figures, she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's four-year-old is 34 days fresh and wears headgear, but recent form figures of 0-7-7-0-5-9 give little confidence; she has no wins or places in good-ground sprint handicaps and would need a dramatically unusual race shape to feature.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Maui Breeze does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and a 34-day break may have freshened her; fifth two starts back is her best recent showing, and she merits consideration from stall two on a respectable speed figure.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners this consistent eight-year-old who won at 7f on good ground last time out and is closely matched on OR; in truth he prefers to come from behind, but with the rear of the field already full of hold-up types he is shown in midfield — he arrives sharp after only seven days, and his best hope is getting first run from a midfield pitch rather than his natural deep hold-up berth.|
runners_data.comment: Monhammer bounced back to winning ways last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving him a live chance from stall four carrying 128 lb; the worry is whether he can back it up on just a week's turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Filey Beach is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 7f handicap and, with no natural rival to push her, she should be able to set a controlled, honest gallop from the front rather than a breakneck tempo. Keep Me Stable will look to sit close behind in a prominent position, and between them they create a steady-to-moderate early pace that is unlikely to stretch the field dramatically through the first half of the race. This shape — a single, uncontested leader dictating on good ground at Musselburgh — typically favours horses who can travel close to the pace and produce a sustained rather than explosive finish, meaning prominent-to-midfield racers get the best of both worlds. Monhammer and Misemerald are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of this field is congested with closers; both are unlikely to secure their natural deep position, and Filey Beach is most likely to control the shape from the front with Keep Me Stable the primary challenger for the early position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Filey Beach Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach leads uncontested and sets a fair, rhythm-based gallop that denies closers a winning burst.
scenarios.body: Filey Beach dictates every yard of the 7f trip on good ground, keeping the pace measured enough to preserve her stamina, and the horses tracking her closely benefit from the economical fractions; the field never gets strung out and the winner comes from the front two or three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Picks Up The Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach hits a flat spot or the gallop quickens sharply in the final two furlongs and the horse sitting second or third kicks clear.
scenarios.body: Keep Me Stable or a horse travelling smoothly in second position seizes the moment when the leader ties up, getting first run through the final furlong on the flat Musselburgh track; good ground rewards a clean, balanced stride and a horse who has conserved energy behind the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Reels Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough that the front pair pay for it, allowing a late finisher to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Misemerald or Chloe's Courage, if able to get closer to their natural hold-up position, would benefit from tiring leaders in the final furlong on a flat track; however this scenario is structurally undermined because the most likely closers are redistributed types not truly racing from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Produces Shock
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners dispute the early lead unexpectedly, burning pace and scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early section would inconvenience Filey Beach and Keep Me Stable who need to travel within themselves, potentially throwing the race open to an unconsidered runner like Maui Breeze who stays out of trouble; this is a low-probability shape given the clear absence of a genuine second pace-maker.

watchPoints.text: Filey Beach's ability to get a clear lead unchallenged is the pivotal factor — if anything crowds her out of the front rank in the early strides, the entire race shape collapses.

Keep Me Stable has the freshest trainer form in the race (Linda Perratt 5/10 in 14 days) and could outrun a price if she travels smoothly in the slipstream of Filey Beach — watch how quickly she improves through the final two furlongs.

Monhammer won last time at this exact trip on good ground and Mulrennan is an aggressive, tactical rider — watch whether he attempts to push forward earlier than his redistribution position suggests, which could inject unexpected pace into the race.

Misemerald has five recent placed efforts and wants more pace than this race is likely to serve up; if she is further back than midfield at halfway she will have too much ground to make up on a flat track.

Going remains good throughout the card with no drift reported across seven races — conditions are consistent and will not deteriorate to offer any unexpected advantage to a horse with a going preference.
